sentences.text:
Bench: Nagesh Bheemapaka
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice Nagesh Bheemapaka
 Writ Petition No. 35235 Of 2024
O R D E R:

Petitioner - Revenue Divisional Officer, Chandur Division seeks, in this Writ Petition, permission for acquisition of Endowments land under RFCTLARR Act, 2013, to an extent of Acs. 81.05 guntas in Survey Nos. 29 (20.32), 30(20.11), 38 (21.09) and 39 (18.33) situated at Madhanapuram Village of Chintapally Mandal of Nalgonda District being vested with title and possession in the name of the 4th respondent - Sri Lakshmi Narsimha Swamy Temple.

2. The case of petitioner is that government had sanctioned Shivannagudem Balancing Reservoir under DLIS Project for development of water source to drought-prone area at Devarakonda and Munugode constituencies.
In the process of land acquisition, Venkepally, Venkepally Thanda and Charlagudem Villages are being submerged, as a result, villagers are totally becoming home and landless.

As per the Act, it is necessary to allot plots under R&R Scheme and to shift the villagers,
who requested plots in the nearby villages.

For which purpose, the Tahsildar, Marriguda Mandal identified the endowment land pertains to Sri Neelakanta Ramaswamy Deval at Indurthy Village of Marriguda Mandal by obtaining permission for acquisition of land vide Writ Petition No. 8450 of 2023, dated 28.03.2023, but the displaced families are not satisfied with the said land.

Hence, the Executive Engineer, Division No. 11, Marriguda Mandal submitted revised requisition proposals with regard to subject land with a request to cancel the previous land acquisition as the proposed land is black cotton and loose soil and not suitable for constructing houses.

3. This Court after hearing learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition as well as learned Government Pleader for Endowments and Sri J. R. Manohar Rao, learned Standing Counsel for the respondent - temple and in view of the order of Division Bench of this Court in Writ Petition No.
10964 of 2022, dated 08.09.2022, dictated order on 19.02.2025.
4.

Then, learned Standing Counsel has brought to the notice of this Court order dated 30.05.2006 in W.P.M.P. No. 13204 of 2006 in Writ Petition No. 10547 of 2006 passed by the Division Bench,
which reads as under:
" This Writ Petition reveals a startling state of affairs.

The lands endowed to the religious institutions which were safe and secure during the alien rule for centuries together, became vulnerable not only to private encroachments but even unlawful The Revenue Divisional Officer vs The State Of Telangana on 7 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120553459/
1 occupation by the Government.

sentences.text: It was in this context that a Division Bench of this Court passed an order on 07.06.2005 in WPMP No. 15055 of 2005 in W.P. No. 11812 of 2005 directing that no sale of endowment land shall be effected, without the permission of this Court, till further orders.
It was also directed that no compromise shall be effected under Section 89 of the A.P. Charitable Hindu Religious Institutions and Endowments Act, 1987 (for short, 'the Act') till further orders.

entities.text: A.P. Charitable Hindu Religious Institutions and Endowments Act, 1987
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The said orders were modified to the effect that if any sale becomes imminent, it shall be done only through public auction.
Despite such specific and unequivocal orders, the taking over of possession of the lands belonging to the temples by the government continued.

Recently, correspondence ensued between District Collector of East Godavari and West Godavari District (Respondents 3 and 4) on the one hand and to the Commissioner of Endowments on the other hand, in the matter of acquisition of endowment lands for providing house sites.
Representations were also made by petitioners herein to the Commissioner of Endowments, second respondent herein.

The second respondent, in turn, addressed letter dated 27.12.2005 to the District Collector, West Godavari District Stating that in view of the orders passed by this Court in WPMP No. 15055 of 2005 in Writ Petition No. 11812 of 2005, any acquisition of endowment lands would be in violation of the said order.

Further, the 2nd respondent addressed letter to the Secretary to Government, Revenue Department i.e. the first respondent herein, on 20.05.2006, narrating the various facts and ultimately impressing upon him to exempt the lands belonging to the temples from acquisition.

Despite the same, respondents 3 and 4 have proceeded to issue notifications, under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, proposing to acquire the lands belonging to various temples, that too by dispensing with the enquiry under Section 5(a) of that Act.

The learned Senior Counsel submits that even for the lands that were acquired several years ago, the compensation has not been paid to the temples and that the present acquisitions of the temple lands in the two Districts would be left without any income.

We are of the prima facie view that the various notifications issued by respondents 3 and 4 proposing to acquire the lands belonging to the temples, amounts to violation of the orders passed by this Court in WPMP No. 15055 of 2005 in WP No. 11812 of 2005.

Hence, the Registry is directed to issue notices to respondents 3 and 4, returnable in four weeks as to why the proceedings under the Contempt of Court Act shall not be initiated against them, for violating the orders in WPMP No. 15055/05 in WP No.
11812 of 2005 dated 17.06.05 as modified thereafter.

We direct that pending further orders, there shall be stay of all further proceedings,
in relation to the acquisition of lands belonging to the temples all over the State, at The Revenue Divisional Officer vs The State Of Telangana on 7 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120553459/

. " 
Since this copy of the order was not brought to the notice of this Court on 19.02.2025 when the order was passed, this Writ Petition is being taken up under the caption 'for being mentioned'.
5.

Here, it is to be noted that Writ Petition No. 10964 of 2022, on which reliance was placed by learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition, was filed seeking permission in terms of the order dated 30.05.2006 in Writ Petition No. 10547 of 2006.

Before filing the said Writ Petition,
petitioner therein approached the Endowments Department for initiation of land acquisition proceedings to which the said Department had given 'no objection' to approach the Court in terms of the order dated 30.05.2006.

The purpose of land acquisition is to acquire land for construction /
excavation of gravity canal namely Kaleswaram Project No. 16 Earth Work at Gundrampally Village of Chityal Mandal, Nalgonda District.
In the instant case, the purpose is to provide house sites to the displaced villagers.

6. Be that as it may, since in Writ Petition No. 10547 of 2006, as extracted supra, pending further orders, the Division Bench directed stay of all further proceedings in relation to acquisition of lands belonging to temples all over the State, at whatever stage they are and any deviation, in this regard would per se be treated as contempt of Court, this Court is not inclined to take a contra decision,
hence, not inclined to accept the contention of learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition.
For the reasons above, the Writ Petition is liable to be dismissed.
7. The Writ Petition is accordingly, dismissed.
No costs.
8. Consequently, Miscellaneous Applications, if any shall stand closed.

NAGESH BHEEMAPAKA, J 07th March 2025 ksld The Revenue Divisional Officer vs The State Of Telangana on 7 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120553459/
